questions.text: When learning how a car engine works, which approach appeals to you more?

options.text: Seeing the actual physical components and how they move.
Understanding the theoretical principles of combustion and energy conversion.

questions.text: In a lecture, you find yourself more engaged by:

options.text: Real-world case studies and historical data.
Conceptual models and metaphorical frameworks.

questions.text: When reading a new instruction manual, you prefer:

options.text: A quick summary of the main steps to get started.
A comprehensive breakdown of every single sub-step and setting.

questions.text: When studying a complex topic, you feel more confident when:

options.text: You grasp the 'big picture' overview first.
You have analyzed every minute detail of the subject.

questions.text: How do you prefer to tackle a difficult new problem?

options.text: Working quietly on my own to process it.
Brainstorming with a group of peers.

questions.text: In a learning environment, you find most value in:

options.text: Independent study and deep focus.
Active discussion and peer feedback loops.
A single evaluation at the end of a long project.
Frequent, instant notifications of whether I am on the right track.

questions.text: When practicing a new skill, which is more motivating?

options.text: Completing a large milestone and then reviewing results.
Receiving real-time 'Correct/Incorrect' prompts after every attempt.

questions.text: When starting a new course, you prefer a curriculum that is:

options.text: A sandbox where I can explore topics in any order.
A strict, step-by-step sequence that must be followed.

questions.text: You feel most productive when your learning path is:

options.text: Flexible and self-directed.
Highly structured and predefined.
